How would you like to use the app?
All data stays exclusively on this device. No server, no automatic detection via Home Assistant, no sync between devices. You can switch to a server at any time later and upload all local data.

Data is stored centrally on a self-hosted Lademonitor server (open source, via Docker) instead of only on the device: automatic charging-session detection via Home Assistant, access from the web UI as well, all devices show the same state.
Like "Connect to your own server", but on the public server at lademonitor.cloud – operation, updates and backups are handled for you. No own server needed.
Please enter the server address in Settings first.
Before you can log a charging session, you need to add at least one vehicle.
All data stays exclusively on this device.

Deletes vehicles, providers, charging locations and charging sessions on this device. Data already synced remains on the server and is fetched back automatically afterwards – changes not yet uploaded are lost.
Irreversibly deletes vehicles, providers, charging locations and charging sessions from this device. There is no other copy.
After signing in you are asked whether your existing local data should be uploaded into the account or deleted from the device. You can switch back to \"Local only\" at any time.
Server responded, but status is not \"ok\".
Please enter the server address first.
Warning: this will also irreversibly delete ALL charging sessions associated with this vehicle.
The external ID cannot be changed after creation.
These prices serve as a suggestion and are updated automatically with every charging session that has a price.
kWh read in the vehicle contain no charging losses. Such sessions are left out of the charging-loss evaluation but still count for the battery index.

Compared with your normal at avg %1$d km/h without heating or cooling, from %2$d drives. The rest covers wind, rain, gradient and driving style.
Avg km/h since charge (trip computer, optional)
Domain of your own Lademonitor server. "https://" is added automatically if you leave it out.
Runs on lademonitor.cloud – operation, updates and backups are handled for you.
Username at least 3 characters, password at least 8 characters. Without an e-mail address everything works as before – only "forgot password" and notifications won\'t.
You can sign in with your username or your e-mail address.
We send a link to reset it. It is valid for one hour and can only be used once.
Careful: resetting signs out all signed-in devices – this app and any Home Assistant integration included.
If there is an account with a confirmed e-mail address for this, the message is on its way.
Check the spam folder too. Open the link in the browser – that is where you set the new password.
What should happen to the data on this device?
There is already data on this device.
There is already data on this device: %1$s.

"Upload" adds it to the account %1$s. "Delete from device" removes it here and loads the state of this account instead – nothing is deleted on the server. "Cancel" signs you out again and leaves everything unchanged.
Your server does not support these features yet. They need Lademonitor Server 0.14.0 or newer.

Needed for "forgot password" and for notifications. Leaving it empty removes the address. The password is a security check: whoever can change the address can afterwards have the password reset. A changed address has to be confirmed again – until then it cannot reset a password.
At least 8 characters. On change the server signs out all devices – this app stays signed in, but Home Assistant and other devices need new access.
Sent by e-mail. Requires SMTP access to be set up on the server.
Enter an e-mail address above so notifications can arrive. In addition, SMTP access has to be set up on the server.

Irrevocably deletes your account and all your data on the server: vehicles, charging sessions, providers, charging locations as well as your MyŠkoda and backup configuration. Home Assistant and other devices are signed out too.
All your data on the server is deleted with it. This cannot be undone.
Your server does not support this feature yet. You need Lademonitor Server 0.16.0 or newer.
No charging sessions with an outside temperature yet. The value is recorded when plugging in – the analysis fills up over the coming weeks.
extrapolated – your data has never seen it this cold
two lines with the lowest consumption at %1$s °C
%1$d charging sessions without a temperature are not included.
The charging sessions are kept – they simply won\'t be attributed to a tire set any more.
What is compared is not the raw seasonal average – that would only measure that winter tires are driven in winter – but the deviation from the consumption curve over outside temperature.
The sets were driven in separate temperature ranges, so the adjusted comparison is an extrapolation.
The sets only overlap by %1$s K of temperature – the figure is mostly an extrapolation.
Left out: %1$d drives without a tire set, %2$d drives spanning a change.

From this date the set applies until the next change follows. That is why there is no end date. The odometer reading makes the mileage exact – without it, it is counted from the attributed drives, and the one drive across the change is missing from it.
* Counted from the attributed drives only – the drive across the change is missing. Enter the odometer reading at the change and the figure becomes exact.
Record the set that is fitted right now – with the date it was mounted, even if that was a year ago, and the odometer reading from back then if you can still find it.

Drives BEFORE that date stay without a tire set – the app has no idea what was fitted then. When guessing, pick a slightly later date rather than one that is too early: too early attributes other sets\' drives to this one, too late merely leaves a few drives out.
Same size all round? Then the first field is enough. With a staggered fitment it holds the front axle and the one below it the rear axle.
Red markers in the charge bar of the charging session list, e.g. for your minimum and target charge level. Applies to this device only.
For example a subscription with a monthly fee that gets you a cheaper price per kWh.
The fee is split by kWh across the provider’s charging sessions in each period and counts towards total cost, price per kWh and cost per 100 km. The price at the charger stays unchanged.
Every month from the start day, e.g. 3 May–2 June, 3 June–2 July and so on.
Every year from the start day.
A price increase is a new entry from the effective date; set “Cancelled” on the old one.
The provider’s base fee is split by kWh across all of its charging sessions in each period.
Effective price per kWh including the base fee, compared with charging without the tariff
Try out any tariff, including one you don\'t have yet. “Take values from” prefills price, base fee and share from an existing provider. Tap a value to enter it exactly.
The share is the part of your charged energy that would be charged on this tariff. What you charge at home does not count.
from %1$d sessions in the last year
No matching sessions in the last year. Enter the price yourself or check which providers are set to “On the road”.

Automatic: the average you paid per kWh at public chargers over the last 12 months, including base fee shares, weighted by kWh and only for the selected charging type. The provider whose values were taken does not count. All providers with the charging place “On the road” count as public – set it on each provider.
The price per kWh you would pay without this tariff, e.g. the ad-hoc price at the charger.
%1$s kWh per month on the tariff: %2$s plus %3$s base fee
Without charging on the tariff, only the base fee of %1$s per month remains.
Without a comparison price it\'s impossible to say whether the tariff pays off.
Costs %1$s more per month (%2$s instead of %3$s)
Same cost with and without the tariff (%1$s per month)
Not worth it at any mileage: the tariff price is not below the price without tariff.
Without a base fee the tariff pays off from the first kWh.
Worth it from about %1$s per month (%2$s kWh on the tariff)
Worth it from about %1$s kWh per month on the tariff

Uses the saved prices and base fees of this provider.
What the same kilometres would have cost with petrol or diesel, and how much CO₂
There are no charging sessions with an odometer reading in this period.
Kilometres from the odometer readings of your charging sessions, costs including base fees. Sessions without a price (e.g. free charging at work) count as 0 €.
The marker shows a typical value for a comparable combustion car. Maintenance, tax and depreciation are not included.

The default is the German grid mix. Lower it for green electricity or your own solar power. For fuel only combustion counts (%1$s kg per litre), without the upstream chain – the Lifecycle view adds it.

Building the vehicle without its battery counts the same for both (about 7 t CO₂); the EV adds its battery. Studies put that at 60 to 100 kg per kWh. For fuel the upstream chain (extraction, refinery, transport) is added here; for electricity it is already part of the emission factor. Consumption and cost per km come from the period you selected.
Total %1$s instead of %2$s, of which production %3$s instead of %4$s
Per 100 km incl. production: %1$s kg instead of %2$s kg CO₂
Not cleaner in use – the production footprint is never paid back
How much is lost while charging and whether the battery takes less over time
This analysis is computed by the Lademonitor server. It is not available in the “Local only on this device” mode.
This analysis needs Lademonitor server 0.28.0 or newer and a connection to it.
There are no charging sessions with a measured kWh value and enough SoC range yet. Automatically detected sessions do not count, their energy is itself estimated.

Only sessions with a real kWh value (invoice, wallbox, import) and at least %1$d percentage points of SoC range are used. The apparent capacity is what charging from 0 to 100 %% would cost at the meter. The loss is the extra energy compared with the vehicle\'s battery capacity – with an aged battery it comes out slightly too low; the difference between AC and DC is the most reliable part.
%1$d charging sessions not used, %2$d of them with estimated energy
%1$d charging sessions read in the vehicle – they count for the battery index, not for the charging losses
There is not enough data for a history yet (at least three sessions per charging type and two per quarter).
Battery index compared with the start of the records, last quarter
100 % = as at the start of the records. AC and DC are each compared with their own start. Not an absolute state of health (SoH), but it shows whether the battery takes less over time.
Without a battery capacity stored on the vehicle, losses cannot be given in percent.
Cost and energy for the current month and your last charging session.
Open the app once and your figures will appear here.

The last four digits of the DOT number on the sidewall: production week and year (2323 = week 23 of 2023). This gives the tire age – look more closely from 6 years, replace after 10 years at the latest. If the tires of one axle have different dates, enter the older one. When the same set is fitted again, the DOT on one entry is enough.
Optional: the lowest measured depth in mm – or per tire, then the lowest value counts. Both measurements get the date and odometer of this change.
Measure in the main grooves at the shallowest point. The legal minimum is 1.6 mm; at least 3 mm is recommended for summer and 4 mm for winter and all-season tires.
Splits the dashboard into home, work and on the road. In the tariff calculator only providers set to “On the road” count towards the automatic price without tariff.
With a purchase price or lease payment, depreciation or leasing is included in the total costs.
Only needed for used cars - the purchase date is used otherwise.
The suggestion follows a typical residual value curve (75 % after the first year, then -13 % per year) and takes mileage into account. A rough estimate - a fixed amount replaces it.
Lease per month incl. down payment
The down payment is spread over the lease term; without an end date it counts in the first month. The end must not be before the start.
Insurance, tax, maintenance and other costs of this vehicle. Unsaved changes above are discarded.
Add insurance, tax, maintenance, repairs and other expenses - one-off or recurring.
Recurring costs count every month or year from the first payment until the last payment or today. The yearly overview also includes charging and depreciation or leasing.
A yearly amount counts in the month it is due.
The last payment is before the first.
Charging, other costs and depreciation or leasing in the selected period. The figures above remain charging costs only.
Inspection, service, tyre change, insurance and more – with a notification when something is due.
Add a reminder with +, e.g. for the next roadworthiness test or tyre change.
Due by date and/or odometer – whichever comes first. The odometer comes from your charging sessions, the forecast from your mileage over the last 90 days.
No due date or odometer set
Without a repeat the reminder stays as done.

The template prefills repeat and due values – everything stays editable.
Within the lead time the reminder counts as “due soon” and shows at the top of the dashboard.

Range = usable capacity × (start − end) ÷ consumption. Driving style, route and heating or air conditioning shift the value.
